 WASHINGTON (WKRC) - — BMW has issued a recall of more than 720,000 vehicles over a fire risk.
 BMW has issued a park-outside recall for 720,796 vehicles because a water pump electrical connector could short-circuit and cause a fire while the vehicle is parked and turned off, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA). Owners are advised to park affected vehicles outside and away from buildings and other vehicles until repairs are made. 
 The vehicles were previously recalled in 2024 for a water pump issue and must be repaired again. BMW is aware of about 10 incidents in the United States that may be related to the problem, but no crashes or injuries have been reported. The incidents involved vehicles repaired under the previous recall, NHTSA said. 
 The connector may not be properly sealed, allowing water to reach it and cause a short circuit. A free remedy is being developed and will be available at BMW dealerships, NHTSA said. 
 The affected models are:
 2012-16 BMW 3 Series 
 2012-16 BMW 5 Series 
 2012-15 BMW X1 
 2012-16 BMW Z4 
 2013-17 BMW X3 
 2014-16 BMW 2 Series coupe 
 2014-16 BMW 3 Series sports wagon 
 2014-16 BMW 328xi Gran Turismo 
 2014-16 BMW 4 Series convertible 
 2014-16 BMW 4 Series coupe 
 2015-16 BMW 2 Series convertible 
 2015-16 BMW 4 Series Gran Coupe 
 2015-18 BMW X4 
 2016-18 BMW X5 xDrive40e 
 Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed beginning Dec. 25, 2026. Owners can check their vehicle identification number or license plate number on NHTSA’s recall website starting that day. 
 Owners can call BMW’s recall hotline at 800-525-7417 or NHTSA’s Vehicle Safety Hotline at 888-327-4236. NHTSA also recommends its SaferCar app for recall updates.
